Vite Express MPA Template

Multi Page React Application using Express and Tailwind CSS with Vite

Edit src/App.jsx and save to test HMR.
Click on the Vite, React and Tailwind CSS logos to learn more.

Stack

  • React 19 — one independent root per page, hydrating prerendered markup
  • Vite 8 — dev server and build, one entry per page
  • Tailwind CSS 4 — via @tailwindcss/postcss
  • Express 5 with helmet — serves the build with the cache and security headers a deploy needs
  • ESLint 9 (flat config), Prettier 3 (auto-sorts Tailwind classes), and Vitest 4 with Testing Library

Setup

  1. git clone https://github.com/CharlesInteractive/vite-express-mpa-template.git
  2. Use the Node version pinned in .nvmrc, e.g. nvm use
  3. Run npm install to install all of the project's dependencies
  4. Run the local development server: npm run dev
  5. Build the project for production: npm run build
  6. Serve the build over Express: npm start

Dev Loop

  • npm run dev - dev server with HMR. Client-only, so pages are not prerendered here
  • npm test / npm run test:watch - run the suite once, or re-run it as you edit
  • npm run lint - ESLint at --max-warnings 0, so a warning fails the run
  • npm run format - format with Prettier, which also sorts Tailwind classes
  • npm run build - full production build to dist/: client, then SSR, then prerender
  • npm run preview - serve the production build locally
  • npm start - serve the build over Express, with the cache and security headers a deploy needs

The three build passes also run on their own as build:client, build:ssr and prerender, which is what you want when debugging a build. CI runs lint, test and build but does not check formatting, so run npm run format before committing.

Testing

Vitest and Testing Library run in a jsdom environment. Beyond the component tests, the suite guards this template's invariants: routes stay in sync with the nav and the build entries, every page's prerendered markup hydrates without a mismatch, and the prerender escapes the metadata it injects.

The server has its own tests — security headers, the cache rules, real 404s rather than redirects, path traversal, and the port fallback. They build a temporary dist fixture rather than using a real build, since CI runs the suite before npm run build.

Project structure

src/
├── index.html            # root page (/) — has the prerender markers
├── main.jsx              #   client entry; hydrates the markup
├── App.jsx               #   component + the page's `meta` export
├── routea/               # example pages: index.html + main.jsx +
├── routeb/               #   App.jsx — copy, edit, or delete them
├── routec/
├── components/
│   ├── Header.jsx        # shared nav + logo bar
│   ├── navLinks.js       # the nav links (a "three places" file)
│   └── pathname.js       # usePathname() — browser and prerender
├── entry-server.jsx      # SSR render entry; build-time only
├── reloadOnChunkError.js # stale-deploy reload guard; client-only
├── index.css             # the one stylesheet, imported everywhere
├── assets/               # imported assets (content-hashed)
└── public/               # copied verbatim into dist/

scripts/
├── prerender.js          # build pass 3 — renders pages into dist/
└── prerenderHtml.js      #   its pure HTML transforms (tested)

server.js                 # `npm start` entry — env, listen, shutdown
server/
├── app.js                # createApp() — middleware, static, 404s
├── csp.js                # the CSP (edit this per site)
└── listen.js             # listenWithFallback() — next free port

tests/
├── routes.test.js        # the MPA invariants
├── hydration.test.jsx    # markup hydrates without a mismatch
└── server.test.js        # the server's headers, caching and 404s

vite.config.js            # client build — the page registry
vite.ssr.config.js        # SSR build — entries from vite.config.js
vitest.config.js          # tests run from the repo root
tailwind.config.js        # theme, loaded via @config in index.css

dist/ is build output: git-ignored and wiped on every build, so never edit it by hand — React overwrites anything you change inside #root when it hydrates.

Multi Page Application

Each page is a folder in /src with its own index.html, main.jsx and App.jsx, mounting its own React root — there is no client-side router, so navigation is a full page load. To add one, copy an existing route folder, register it in vite.config.js, and add a nav link in src/components/navLinks.js. A test fails if those three drift apart.

Prerendering

This page is static HTML: npm run build renders every page to real markup and the browser hydrates it, so crawlers and link previews see content rather than an empty root element. The build output is still fully static, so any static host will serve it. Each page exports a meta object from its App.jsx for its title, description and Open Graph tags.

Anything reachable from an App.jsx also runs in Node at build time, so avoid window and document at module scope or during render. If a page cannot be rendered the build fails, rather than quietly shipping a blank one.

Tailwind CSS

The default project is styled with preconfigured Tailwind directives and layers. Learn more about Tailwind CSS here.

A font pack is also included (Nunito Sans) along with its Open Font License.

Server

npm start serves dist/ over Express with the headers a production deploy needs. npm run start:watch does the same and restarts when a server file changes (Node's built-in --watch, no nodemon). Run npm run build first — the server exits with a clear message rather than serving 404s if dist/ is missing.

  • server.js — entry: env parsing, preflight check, listen, logging, graceful shutdown
  • server/app.js — createApp(): middleware, static mounts, the 404 and error handlers
  • server/csp.js — the Content-Security-Policy, the one file you edit per site
  • server/listen.js — listenWithFallback(), the port walk

Configuration is environment variables: PORT (defaults to 8006; an unparseable value exits 1 rather than silently binding elsewhere), HOST (defaults to 0.0.0.0), NODE_ENV (production enables HSTS and upgrade-insecure-requests), and TRUST_PROXY for running behind a reverse proxy.

If the port is busy the server takes the next one — 8006, 8007, and so on for up to ten attempts — and logs where it landed. EACCES is not retried: a privileged port is a permissions problem that the next port up will not fix.

Headers come from helmet. HTML is served no-cache, /assets/* (content-hashed) immutable for a year, and /fonts/* for a week. An unknown path gets a real 404 — never a redirect to /, which would hand an HTML body to a request for a missing chunk and break the stale-deploy recovery described above.

One thing to know before adding analytics: script-src carries no 'unsafe-inline'. This template's build emits zero inline scripts, so the strict policy costs nothing — but Google Tag Manager's container snippet and some AdSense paths are inline and will be blocked. server/csp.js documents both ways out, and is also where you add any third-party script, font, embed or analytics host.

Deployment

Serve the HTML entries with Cache-Control: no-cache so browsers always get markup that matches the current asset hashes; the hashed files under dist/assets/ can be cached indefinitely.

Two ways to get that right: hand dist/ to a static host and configure the headers there, or run npm start — an Express server that serves the build with those cache rules, a Content-Security-Policy and the rest of the security headers already applied. It takes the next free port if the one it wants is busy.
